reuse.why: Link rules are factored into shared helpers (assertUpgradingAccountOpen, releaseBankAccountFromOtherAccounts, clearAccountBankLink shared with unlinkAccount), but the Fintegra provider is added by copying the existing link and download functions rather than reusing a common path.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount repeats the ~60-line create-or-upgrade/sync/notify body of the other link functions, downloadFintegraTransactions is a renamed copy of downloadAkahuTransactions, and the same two guard calls are pasted into all six link functions.

placement.why: Rules sit in server/accounts/app.ts next to the link handlers, the download in sync.ts, the URL in server-config and the type in types/models, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Covers the four steps; the desktop-client edits are the minimum needed for the new provider key to type-check.

maintainability.why: Guard helpers are clear, but per-provider guard boilerplate instead of one wrapper, and another copied link/download pair, leave six places to keep in sync.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All link handlers call the shared guards; unlinkAccount uses clearAccountBankLink

disguised_duplication.where: sync.ts downloadFintegraTransactions is downloadAkahuTransactions renamed and slightly trimmed; app.ts linkFintegraAccount reshapes the akahu/simplefin link body

abstraction_drift.where: releaseBankAccountFromOtherAccounts takes a replaceExistingLink flag that switches it between refusing and clearing holders; every link handler calls it directly
